sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned HCGP for respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2, who is served in the matter has remained unrepresented before this Court.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner had earlier approached this Court in Crl.P.No.8191/2024 and the said petition was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to the petitioner to file a fresh petition after examination of the victim girl is completed before the Trial Court.
He submits that victim girl/CW1 has been examined before the Trial Court as PW1 and she has not supported the case of the prosecution.
Petitioner, who has no other criminal antecedents is in custody from 12.12.2023.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
4. Per contra, learned HCGP does not dispute the submission made by learned counsel for the petitioner.
5. In the present case, petitioner has been arrested and remanded to judicial custody on 12.12.2023.

Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed against him for the aforesaid Shri Rajesh B S vs State Of Karnataka on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163716772/

sentences.text: His earlier bail application in Crl.P.No.8191/2024 was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to the petitioner to approach this Court after examination of the victim girl/CW1 is completed before the Trial Court.
Victim girl has been examined before the Trial Court as PW1.
The deposition of PW1 would go to show that she has completely NC: 2025:KHC:5426 turned hostile to the case of the prosecution and therefore, she was cross-examined by the Public Prosecutor.
Petitioner, who is aged about 20 years, having no criminal antecedents
is in custody from 12.12.2023.

Considering the fact that victim girl has turned hostile to the case of the prosecution and also taking into consideration the period of incarceration of the petitioner, I am of the opinion that his prayer for grant of regular bail needs to be answered affirmatively.
Accordingly, the following order:-
6. The petition is allowed.
